summary: Smith Ridge L-4 lookout, Umpqua NF: dated 1936 or 1942 by different sources, gone after 1967. A Forest Service trail climbs to the site.

facts.design: L-4 cab on a short pole tower
facts.status_note: Lookout gone after 1967 (sources say removed or destroyed); the site is reached on foot.
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Umpqua National Forest

visit.trail_note: Smith Ridge Trail #1561 climbs steeply to the site; expect snow from mid-to-late fall through early-to-mid spring

access.note: Forest Service trail to the site; parking is a small turnout at the end of Forest Road 2813

events.note: L-4 cab built atop a short tower, enclosed to create a storage area (Forest Lookouts history)
College students stationed at Umpqua lookout posts that summer (News-Review, August 4, 1962); Smith Ridge listed
Register says removed; firelookout.com says destroyed

evidence.quote: Built in 1936, this 8' pole L-4 tower was removed in 1967.

evidence.supports: L-4 cab 1942 on a short tower, enclosed as storage
evidence.quote: 1942: An L-4 lookout cab was constructed atop a short tower. The tower was enclosed to create a storage area.

evidence.supports: August 4, 1962 News-Review item: college students stationed at Umpqua lookout posts in summer 1962, Smith Ridge among them
evidence.quote: August 4, 1962: The line up of college students stationed this summer at lookout posts in the Umpqua National Forest: Smith Ridge

evidence.supports: Umpqua National Forest, Douglas County, Oregon location
evidence.quote: Umpqua National Forest Douglas County, Oregon

evidence.supports: trail climbs to site of former lookout, gone; views into Dumont and Straight Creek drainages
evidence.quote: This steep trail switchbacks up to the site of a former fire detection lookout. The lookout is gone, but the views are great, into the Dumont Creek drainage and Straight Creek drainage.

evidence.supports: snow cover from mid-to-late fall through early-to-mid spring
evidence.quote: From mid-to-late Fall through early-to-mid Spring expect that this trail will have snow cover.

evidence.supports: Forest Road 2813 about 8 miles to trailhead
evidence.quote: Turn left onto Forest Road 2813 and continue for approximately 8 miles.

evidence.supports: parking limited to a small turnout
evidence.quote: Parking is limited to a small turnout.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the tower was removed in 1967 and firelookout.com says it was destroyed that year. Both say it was gone by 1967; the story uses the register's word.

sources.title: Smith Ridge Trail
sources.publisher: USDA Forest Service, Umpqua National Forest

notes_for_editor: Build date unresolved: 1936 (register, firelookout.com) against 1942 (Forest Lookouts history, an L-4 cab on a short tower). The register's own photo caption reads 'Smith Ridge Lookout 1942', which may fit the later cab; the story reports both dates and does not choose. The Forest Service trail page is the only current source and describes the site, not any remains. Access is by trail on Forest Service land; the page does not mention closures.
